summary: Adds an admin endpoint that deletes one user by id and an endpoint that purges a list of users.

findings.title: User delete route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route omits the requireAdmin middleware that its sibling routes use. Any caller can reach db.removeUser with an arbitrary id.
findings.consequence: Any client that reaches the server can delete any user account. The attacker can enumerate ids to wipe the user table.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route, as the GET and purge routes do.

findings.title: Purge deletes run as floating promises
findings.problem: The forEach callback returns promises that the purge handler never awaits or catches. The handler reports ids.length as removed before any delete finishes.
findings.consequence: db.removeUser throws for an unknown id, so one bad id causes an unhandled rejection that crashes the Node process. The removed count is also wrong when deletes fail.
findings.fix: Await the deletes with Promise.allSettled and report the number that succeeded.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete endpoints have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds two delete endpoints with new auth and error paths. The repository contains no test that exercises them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in access control or purge error handling will go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for the unauthorized delete, the purge with an unknown id, and the purge count.
